## D260 · 2026-11-02 · A judgement is a forecast against a reference: the rung the evidence in force makes most likely, judged against what the market expects; the answer states the reference and the implied outcome (judging-v6)

- Alex, 2026-11-02, asked whether the judge's stance should stay an absolute-band lookup (the current reading) or be judged relative to expectations: "门槛没有标准，按照你作为 hedge fund analyst 的认识来定". Decided by Claude under that delegation: the definition below is Claude's analyst judgement, recorded as such, not Alex's words.
- Mechanism (arm 4 draw 1, all 356 judgements read, `research/2026-11-01-e2e-loop/review-2026-11-02.md` §7 and `proof-judging-v6.txt`): 8 of 314 later judgements moved a rung and 320 of 356 reasons say "remains"; the FY2027 total revenue question was judged 12 times at neutral while its upward pushes grew from 1 to 35, every reason "the $392 billion estimate is inside the band … does not establish $400 billion"; the gross-margin judgement wrote "leans toward rung 2 but does not warrant moving"; the 2027 hyperscaler-capex theme stayed below the band management's own forecast names because the forecast "is not fact". The judging-v5 prompt asked the judge to "be precise about what is established" and said only fact can establish a rung: the model read "established" as the bar for leaving a rung and the consensus figure as the anchor. A second cause stays open: the ladder's neutral band is written at opening without naming what it compares against (PRD 06 ladder rule 2 asks for it); that is the extraction's rule and is not changed here.
- Decided, the analyst's rule: (1) the rung is a forecast, the outcome the evidence in force makes most likely at the due date, not the one it has proved; "not established" is a statement of confidence, never a reason to stay. (2) The reference is what the market expects: consensus, the company's guidance, the stated plan or deadline; a consensus or guidance figure alone keeps the judgement at the reference's rung and, once other evidence has arrived, is never the reason to stay. (3) The judge derives the outcome the evidence implies (reported figures and guidance give a run-rate; a quantified revision, a customer's demand number, a supplier's constraint, a confirmed delay or cancellation shift it), checks it against the dependencies' conclusions (a part cannot exceed its whole; a figure spanning several periods or products gives the question only its share), compares it with the rung boundaries and moves when it crosses one. (4) Weight follows tier and novelty: fact fixes what is known; party statements are the strongest forecast input; third-party views and rumours move the forecast in proportion to their specificity; a repeat, another outlet or an opinion with no new fact or calculation moves nothing. (5) The answer states `reference` and `implied_outcome` as required fields from `judging-v6` (`judging.schema_for`; code refuses an empty one; stored beside the rung in `judgements.reference` / `implied_outcome`; a ledger written before v6 gains the columns at its first write), so the D3 stance gold can read the reasoning, not only the rung. Written where the judgement is specified: PRD 06 State rules (`docs/system-design/new-facts.js` STATE_RULES, the generated block) and this record.
- Proof (`proof-judging-v6.txt`, `proof-judging-v6b.txt`: the last stored judgement request of 14 theses of arm 4 draw 1 re-sent once each under v6 and read beside the stored v5 answers, about a cent): every answer names the reference and derives the implied outcome. Six rungs moved against the stored ones: non-GAAP gross margin 3 → 2 (Q1 reported 75% and Q2 guided 75% sit on the rung-2 boundary), 2027 hyperscaler capex 4 → 5 (management's own "more than $1 trillion"), China accelerator share 4 → 5 (share "fallen to zero"), China H200 authorization No → Yes (a reported plan to permit named firms and reported progress in reviews, six months before the deadline), Data Center revenue 2 → 3 ($355–360 billion derived from Q1 and the total-revenue proxy, below the $360 billion boundary), Blackwell+Rubin revenue 2 → 1 in the first send by annualising a two-year "$1 trillion visibility" figure to $545 billion, a part above its whole: clause (3)'s consistency check was added for it and the re-send gives rung 2 ($320–360 billion, a share of the Data Center segment). Total revenue stays at 3 with the arithmetic shown (H1 $172.6 billion from Q1 and the Q2 guide; $400 billion needs more than $227 billion in H2). Prompt 2,453 → 3,782 characters: the request defined neither what a rung means nor a reference and its "established" wording forced the defect; the two sentences that carried it were cut. Configuration `poc-v90` (poc-v89 with judging-v6); the default stays `poc-v69`. Tests: `tests/test_stance_fields.py`. Measured by re-sent stored requests, not by an arm (Alex: "不要再跑这些有的没的臂了").

## D263 · 2026-11-02 · The judge is written to the frozen gold's own reasoning (judging-v7, poc-v91); a gap to the gold is closed in the judge, not re-measured

The regression read matter by matter: 19 supporting matters v94 wrote in at least two draws are absent, nearly all named partnerships or adoptions with no size (a reactor maker's partnership, a platform made free, a game platform's support, a data firm's collaboration, humanoid-robot partners); the cause is my own drift: the condition written into the role's adoption clause, the check's row 7 and the T6 block, "a named party and a size or date", is stricter than standard 5.1 kind 2's "a size, date or name" (any one). Corrected as extraction v76 / `poc/config/poc-v96.json` (the three places in the standard's words; nothing else changes) and proved on the 14 articles of the lost matters, three sends each (`proof-v76-adoption.txt`): their 36 supporting matters present 68 times over v94's three draws against 60 over v96's three sends, 6 still never, and the same articles' gold not-kept statements written 48 → 60 (partner releases and company blogs: the wider condition lets part of their noise back). The model's own account on the residue class under v95 (`probe-v75-residue.txt`, seven cases): in five of six omissions it concedes on re-reading that the row's boundary keeps the statement (a memory maker's revenue, a customer's price rises, two memory suppliers' expansions, a rack supplier's chairman, named partner integrations); the mechanism is the check's procedure, the model sorts a statement into a reject row and stops, not any one sentence; the structural fix proposed, not built: a closed classification of each statement's relation to the company (its own, supplier, customer, competitor, partner, regulator, analyst, none) as a schema field with examples, the keep decision following from relation and scale. ## D269 · 2026-11-03 · The second prompt audit, on the v95 draw: the one large class left is a precedence contradiction; the sentence-level fix (v77) is a patch and is not kept; the next step is structural

- Alex: "你跑一下我刚才写的skill，深度的判断下。我不要再全部重跑了，你帮我训读的跑完skill看下怎么快速改进improve". The skill ran on `arms/r8-audit-v95/d1` ($0, `design-v72.md` §14): the request read whole (the keep decision sits in the role's walk and reject list, the check's header and rows, and the links field), the failure lists (core 78 reach / 7 not written / 1 dropped; supporting 88 / 57 / 6; written noise 36 with no dominant row; 5 no-home drops of another-period estimates; one doubtful tier in fifteen; 5 quote refusals). The one large class, 57 of 148 supporting matters never written, maps to a precedence contradiction: the role's walk says "take it only when it has a kind and nothing on the list applies" (the reject list has the last word) while the check's header says "what a line says it does not cover goes to the check" (the exceptions have the last word); the model follows the role's order and stops at the first reject line; its own account conceded the exception in five of six cases.
- Built and proved, not kept: `role-v77.txt` / `review-v77.txt` / `poc/config/poc-v97.json` state one precedence (exceptions read before the line; a statement with a kind stays unless a line names it and no exception sends it back), ask the walk to name the party's relation to the company, and cut "Fitting one of the four kinds does not keep an item" (+238 and +53 characters). On the 41 supporting matters v94 wrote in at most one draw (29 articles, three sends, sent twice): presences 12 → 71 and 64 (v75: 31), matters still never written 7 and 13 (v75: 23), but the same articles' gold not-kept statements written 27 → 78 and 82 (v75: 35), spread over the retold-arrangement row (13), common knowledge (7), product details (7), other companies' matters with no path (4) and a tail. A one-for-one trade of supporting matters for noise is a patch (AGENTS §7.2), so v77 is recorded and not adopted; the candidate stays poc-v96.
- What the audit concludes: sentence-level fixes on this class have reached their limit; "is it new" and "is there a path" are judgements the model makes in passing while reading the list, and reordering the list moves both recall and noise together. The structural fix to design next (AGENTS §2 tables, $0 proof on the stored articles, no run): two closed-set fields per statement in the schema, the party's relation to the company (its own, supplier, customer, competitor, partner, regulator, analyst or outlet, none) and what is new (a new step, figure, forecast or plan, policy step, judgement, or a retelling), with the keep rule derived from them and the standard's scale condition, and the check's rows rewritten as the boundaries of those classes; this is what v71's free-text `new_in_it` and `moves` fields lacked (no closed set, no rule reading them). poc-v94 stays the default.

Control/examples: 91/99 versus 89/99 complete requirements, 6/8 versus 7/8 delivered answers, 71/99 versus 80/99 delivered complete requirements. ## D350 · 2026-10-27 · Audit actual source/output before drawing model-quality conclusions

- Alex requests direct examination of failures rather than benchmark-driven tuning. [The audit](research/2026-10-27-evaluation-audit/results.md) rereads the three sources and D349 outputs, reviews all 65 error /7 disputed record labels and 18 non-pass requirements, and checks matching historical scoring classes. No new model calls or prompt changes.
- Withdraw D349's “examples did not improve semantic quality” interpretation: two quarter-number deductions exceeded the frozen clause; source-faithful supply-chain paraphrases were penalized inconsistently in 12 requirements across D347–D349. Correcting only five identified D349 clause decisions would reverse the old numerical order. This sensitivity exercise does not adopt a new score or declare examples better. Historic gold, judgments, scores and outputs remain unchanged and are annotated as superseded interpretations.
- Distinguish argument preservation from independent-record usability, field-contract compliance and writer delivery. A conditional valuation split across records often retained the premises in the same answer; that does not establish safe downstream use or true information loss. The current research boundary returns the complete source packet; no actual downstream selection/consolidation reader was tested by these prompt comparisons.
- Three invalid references among 582 D349 reference fields blocked 63 records. Exact manual lexical corrections on copies let all three answers through the unchanged writer without modifying summaries. This diagnoses failure amplification, not semantic correctness and not permission to relax the writer. Source-field errors, non-temporal time fields, unsupported fiscal anchors and some attribution errors remain real.
- Review explicit evaluation units and ambiguous gold before another comparison. Use an unexposed full article with a reference prepared before its model output, then exercise the actual downstream reader. No production contract, default, gold replacement, spending increase or paid restart is adopted by this audit.

## D352 · 2026-10-27 · TrueNorth event index backfilled by identity; the result is a measurement, not a replacement

- Alex: "你用一下我们的truenorth-api 不是有个event endpoint 吗，你也backfill 一发nvidia, geopolitcs, chip supply chain 相关的数据到我们这个clean source db. 现在就做".
- Built: `harvest_truenorth.py --events` over the window with per-topic selectors in `topics.json` (`truenorth`: asset ids and text queries); `assemble.truenorth_story_topics` labels a story by identity only (the asset selector that found it, or the asset ids the story carries); a text-query hit with no listed asset id is not an item, because the index matches any word and such hits were mostly off topic. New databases `items-nvda-2026-07-01-10-27-tn.page.sqlite` / `-tn.sqlite` by the D351 chain; the canonical database is not replaced.
- Measured ([results](research/2026-10-27-truenorth-events/results.md)): the index starts 2026-07-23; 708 story rows enter, 72 fed; 83% of links are benzinga.com, which blocks the fetcher, so the rest are provider summaries (not fed, D351/Alex 2026-10-23: original documents only); geopolitics cannot be selected by identity beyond crude oil. Alex (2026-10-27): "你记录下truenorth 的库不太能用的原因吧，然后先别管他了". Set aside; the backfilled databases stay as a record, the canonical database is unchanged, and no further work goes to this source.
- Why the TrueNorth event index is not usable as a source, in four measured facts: (1) no article text: `include_body` returns nothing and no tool returns an article, and 83% of the links are benzinga.com, which blocks the fetcher (403 on 576 of 576), so 636 of 708 stories are a title and a summary only; (2) no topic selection: text queries match any word (random samples of the export-control, tariff and supply-chain hits were mostly off topic) and the `topic` filter accepts no known value, so geopolitics cannot be selected except through an asset id such as crude oil; (3) no history: the index starts 2026-07-23, so a window from July 1 loses three weeks; (4) thin: 283 NVIDIA stories and about 375 supply-chain stories in three months against 27,000 Google News listings in the same window, with 70% of them from one publisher.

  set the method on 2026-11-04 ("We need to validate the hypothesis in a very simple way and to make sure that it works on a high level before we
  dive into do the full analysis stability test"; "如果有什么不符合hypothesis 的地方你需要终止然后和我说我们重新评估"), and closed it: "那就1吧"
  (option 1: close the topic, record the pattern as a known defect, go to step 5).
- What was found (`research/2026-11-03-filing/report.html`, `log.md` rows 1–17): three rounds of Claude–Codex review converged on "the question
  definition is too narrow"; an independent challenge and the first stored-request test refuted it (the earlier version's definition was already
  broad; the same request gives different filings from send to send). Two cheap tests of fixes did not fit their hypotheses and stopped: removing the
  total-revenue fallback alone leaves good indirect evidence unlinked; teaching "one fact, two uses" made the model add a second company-revenue
  question instead. A size measurement per class (six observations per fact) and a wider check before test 3 put filing at about 85% right:
  the company's own quarterly figures 82%, forecasts 91%, other companies' figures 84% on fourteen facts.

  designer's revenue) is filed under the company's revenue questions instead of the share, capital-spending or custom-chip question it informs;
  the model reads it as "what it means for the company" and the fallback sentence sends it there; the custom-chip question lost its main evidence
  this way in the frozen draws. (2) Share facts are often not written at all (the gold's core "China share fallen to zero" in none of six
  observations): an extraction recall miss, not filing. (3) The model files only relations an article states; one needing industry knowledge (a
  chip designer's AI revenue as a measure of cloud providers' custom-chip spending) is not made unless the article says it.

## D356 · 2026-11-04 · Step 5: closing at the due day is pull mode's; no separate final verdict, no day-end re-judging, due days after publication, the frozen rung recorded and shown

- Alex: "按照你的4个建议收尾一次，清晰的write the design, 文档，确保我们的一致性，然后你也需要清理repo不要让旧的东西影响我们整个sanity". The four leans he
  accepts are Claude's of the same day, on D54's open questions:
  1. **No separate final review before closing.** Each day's judgement already reads the evidence in force (D198's window), so a review at
     the due day repeats it. The final verdict is no longer a step; D29's earlier draft (verification conditions, confirmed/falsified/expired,
     premises, triggers) is retired. Config's `final_verdict` setting stays in the frozen configurations (D274) and is read by no step.
  2. **No day-end re-judging without new evidence.** Pull mode closes the questions that are due and does nothing else at day end; it is
     revisited when a case is named.
  3. **A due day falls on or after the day the result is published,** set when the question is opened (the opening rule "set the due date
     when the question can be resolved", 06-views). A question whose result is still unknown on its due day closes at its state like any other;
     nothing waits (D54).
  4. **The frozen rung is recorded and shown, never a gate** (AGENTS §8). The closing record names the rung the question froze at; a question
     never judged closes with "no data to verify". Its judgement history, already stored and served, shows how the state moved up to the close.
     Telling a closing rung that reflects the published result from one that is still a forecast is not built until the first real due day
     (2026-12-31) gives a case.
- Built: `src/hivemind/pull.py` writes the closing record (rung and label, or "no data to verify"); `tests/test_pull.py` proves it (mutants:
  the first judgement instead of the last, the no-data branch removed). A $0 check on a copy of the frozen first draw with the day set to
  2027-03-01 closed the thirteen questions due by then at their last rung, and a dependent question's judging request shows the closed question
  with its last conclusion; two questions never judged closed with no state, which this change marks.
- Pages: PRD 07 becomes the closing contract (the D29 draft is removed from it; Git keeps it), PRD 08 states what pull mode does, the design
  page's two nodes and the closing drill-down say the same, and `docs/check.py` now reads both PRDs and both nodes in the wording check.
- Not built, not decided: fetching settlement figures (prices, filings) from a source; Claude's earlier daily duplicate check.
- After a read-only Codex review the same day, two gaps between this decision and the product were closed. (1) A closing on a day without
  items took the day's last sequence number, which belonged to the day before, so the question page showed the question closed a day
  early; pull mode now records the day under a sequence number of its own when it closes something on such a day (`pull.closing_sequence`).
  Census: 0 of the 42 day ends of the three frozen draws were affected, and 1 of the 119 days of the stored news window has no items
  (2026-10-27); in production a holiday is enough. (2) The closing record was served but never shown: the question page now shows it

  fails on its mutant (the old numbering; the record shown while the question is open).

## D369 · 2026-11-05 UTC · Capture core and supporting evidence without a strict boundary; retain the MXC case

- Alex: “我觉得往后核心和辅助其实只要是捕捉到就好，不用真的严格区分了，把它作为decision, 因为这两个边界很模糊，我觉得没必要纠结到死” and “我觉得留下辅助，只要LLM自己的判断是相关且逻辑清晰就好”.
- For future extraction evaluation, evidence that the standard would keep as core or supporting is assessed together for whether it was captured. Do not make a hard pass/fail distinction between those two weights. This does not establish that every statement is relevant, change the optional or excluded boundary, replace source tiers, or remove checks for meaning, attribution, uncertainty, errors and delivery. Historical scores retain their original definitions and are not compared as if this was their ruler.
- In the reviewed Microsoft MXC example, retain the reported announcement as supporting evidence. The model may judge relevance using a clear logical connection; an unquantified indirect connection is not automatically rejected. A proposed NVIDIA demand effect is an inference, not a fact attributed to Microsoft; the article does not say MXC requires NVIDIA hardware. This is not permission to accept unrelated material or to hard-code a list or new mandatory output field.
- The frozen standard v5, golden-v5, seeds and historical results remain byte-for-byte unchanged (D261/D262). Applying this decision to a new real-article gold requires a separate evaluation version under D261. Alex asked for a real-article gold; treating that as authorization to develop the separate version is an implementation interpretation, not a quotation from his decision. It still needs its own traced references, independent review and Alex's sign-off before scoring. The experimental evidence comparison has not been sent.

## D372 · 2026-11-05 UTC · Score future evidence by usefulness, not core versus supporting

- Alex: “我们金标的打分只要量化好有帮助/没帮助就好，至于是核心还是辅助我们不用特别分开因为这样造成不必要的ambiguity,这是之后量测的准则你记录好”.
- For future evidence measurement, the scoring distinction is whether a statement is helpful or not helpful to the investment-research task. Do not separately classify or score helpful evidence as core versus supporting. Quantify useful evidence captured or missed and unhelpful evidence returned, with the evaluated population and counting unit stated; inspect the source and output, not only aggregate numbers. A statement's source tier and faithful attribution, conditions and dates remain separate properties, not a proxy for usefulness.
- This amends D369's combined reporting: the future scoring categories are helpful / not helpful, not core / supporting. It does not silently reclassify old optional or excluded cases, settle the separate open question about three question-gold items, or authorize invented shortcut rules. A new reference must decide usefulness from the actual source under the new criterion, with its unit and decisions documented and reviewed.
- This is Alex's decision to open the changed evaluation criterion under D261. Frozen standard and golden-v5 files and historical scores are not edited or relabelled. Any new ruler/gold is a distinct version derived from source, independently reviewed and signed before scoring; historical and new-version scores are never represented as directly comparable. ## D389 · 2026-11-09 · An unsigned obligation is large enough for its own signing question at about 5% of the company's annual profit

- Asked: "“多大算大”用什么尺寸？" The options were 5% of a year's profit (recommended), 1% of annual revenue, or no threshold and stop.
  Alex chose "一年利润的 5% (Recommended)", whose stated terms were:
  - "单笔未签承诺约达到公司一年利润的 5% 才单独开'会不会签'（亏损公司另议）";
  - "金额不知道的，比如俄亥俄，仍按文章描述定性判断";
  - "公司最近一年利润作为固定资料交给小步骤".
- **Decided.** Under D388, a single unsigned obligation is large enough for its own signing question when its stated amount is about 5%
  or more of the company's most recent annual profit. An obligation whose amount is not stated is judged qualitatively from what the
  item states. The company's most recent annual profit is supplied to the step as fixed input, with its source. A loss-making company
  is not covered and is decided when one arises.
- **Why.** In the focused D388 call, the same $2bn stake opened in 0 of 3 draws under one wording and 3 of 3 under another, and a
  $2.5–3bn stake opened in 6 of 6, even when compared with stated revenue (round log §§54–55). The standard's "large enough to change"
  (D248 boundary 6) had no anchor the model applied consistently. The 5% line agrees with every known verdict:
  - small: about $2bn, $2.5–3bn, Intel's $5bn;
  - open: Hugging Face at $12.9bn.
- **Scope.** It applies to the focused D388 step under test. It enters the clean-arch PRD only if that step is adopted. The frozen
  extraction standard and gold are unchanged (AGENTS §7.1).

## D390 · 2026-11-09 · A plan counts as undertaken once a deal under it is reported signed

- Asked: "一个合作计划，什么时候算'已经启动'（只跟踪总额，不再问'会不会签'）？" The options were: started once a deal under it is

  (Recommended)", whose stated terms were:

    - stop.

- **Decided:**
  - Three unseeded clean draws (c8 from an empty library) on v108's 243 items.
  - Each run's opened questions are matched to the ruler questions by the frozen rule, through an independent reading, before any
    judging.
  - The matched questions are judged by the frozen judge through the adapter and scored by the frozen scorer. The graded subset is q04,
    q05, q08, q09, q13, q18 and q23; every other question is reported.
  - The adapter extension and the launcher get tests and a council read before the send.

    - improve opening, at the risk of tuning to these cases;
    - stop.

## D397 · 2026-11-10 · A topic that asks more than one thing gets one judged question; the other parts are shown as not judged

- **Asked**, after the review council on the Step 4 design (round log §69; two blind readers found 12 to 16 of the 34 opened theses
  asking more than one thing): "新系统自己开的 34 道题里，有 12–16 道一题问了两件事（例如：英伟达会不会给 OpenAI 的俄亥俄数据中心签担保——金额多少？）。给这种题写答案分段时，怎么处理？"
  - Options:
    - judge only the main thing and show the rest as not judged (recommended). The option stated its costs: those parts have no
      answer for now; three memory topics with no main part get no answer; and it departs from his 2026-10-20 rule that a question
      looks at one thing and two things are two questions (D38), recorded as a gap to fill;
    - split into two questions, each judged, as D38 says;
    - do not judge such a topic until Step 1 opens it as one thing.
  - Alex: "只判主要那件 (Recommended)".
- **Decided:**
  - In the clean Step 4's ladder step, a thesis gets at most one judged question: the part its `outcome` names. Every other part of
    its wording is listed and shown beside the answer as not judged.
  - A thesis with no main part gets no judged question, with the reason recorded.
  - For a topic that holds two real bets this departs from D38 until splitting is built. It is an open defect, sized by the first
    test: readers mark each part left out as a bet an analyst would hold or not.
- **Scope:** the clean path's ladder step only. D38 stands for production.

## D398 · 2026-11-10 · The clean ladder step carries D186: ranges against the reference, the favourable end registered, labels by code

- **Asked**, with the census of production's own ladders (one request, the same in three draws, gave three different ladders, one
  with its direction reversed): "你 10 月 26 日定过、11 月 5 日说“我们要做”的那条规矩还没实现：答案分段要对着市场预期或公司指引写成“高于／接近／低于”，并且每道题登记“数字越高对公司是好还是坏”。新做的“定档”这一步要不要直接带上它？"
  - Options:
    - both halves here (recommended). The option stated its costs: 7 to 9 of 18 number questions have no reference figure in their
      opening article, so their ranges are the model's estimate and are marked "no reference"; a direction can still be registered

    - the direction half only;
    - not here: write ladders as production does, and leave D186 to a later version.
  - Alex: "两半都带上 (Recommended)".
- **Decided:**
  - The clean ladder step builds D186 in full. The model states the reference the opening article gives and, for a company's figure,
    which end is good for the business, with one sentence why. Code orders and labels the rungs from that end, writes each range's
    text from its bounds, and checks that a stated reference value lies in the middle range.
  - The reference is what D260 lists: a consensus, the company's guidance, the stated plan or deadline. This is wider than D186's
    word "guidance"; the question put to him said "市场预期或公司指引".

- **Scope:** the clean path's ladder step. D368 item 1 still holds for the next production extraction version.

- **Asked**, after three hand-written five-state ladders had each shown a gap or an overlap and three built by a construction had

## D401 · 2026-11-10 · Once a review finds nothing serious, build the ladder step and run Stage A without asking again

## D403 · 2026-11-10 · An event's due day is a stated date or the last day of the thesis's period; the model picks no other day

## D405 · 2026-11-10 · A reference's words must be the article's own, in one unbroken passage; otherwise the answer is sent back once

    wrong and writes again once; wrong twice, no question is written; no quote with a word left out is ever taken for the

## D408 · 2026-11-10 · Stage A missed its lines: stay at the ladder step, fix the event answers first, validate at no cost, then run the same Stage A once more

## D409 · 2026-11-10 · An event is answered in three outcomes: it happened, it is ruled out, or neither by the due day

- **Asked:** "事件类的题（比如“监管会不会批准”“调查会不会罚款”），答案要分几种结局？现在让模型自己写五种状态，这是最容易出漏洞的地方：两家读者都认定的 7 个漏洞里，6 个出在第四、第五种状态的细分上。"
  - Options: three outcomes (recommended): "发生了 / 明确落空（被否决、被放弃）/ 到期还没结果。第三种由程序写成“前两种都不是”，所以不会有遗漏。保住了“否决”和“还在等”的区别；更细的区别（如“附条件批准”）列为“不判”。这是我的建议，写法还要先免费验证。"; yes or no only (the simplest; "rejected" and "still waiting" become one No, which the council held loses a difference an analyst cares about); several outcomes where they are needed, the number not fixed (the council's recommendation; a new structure, one more round of design).
  - Alex: "分三种 (Recommended)".
- **Decided:** on the clean ladder step an event's answer has at most three outcomes: the event has happened by the due day; the
  event is ruled out (decided against, abandoned); neither. The third is written by code as "neither of the two holds", so no
  outcome is without a rung. A finer difference (an approval with conditions against one without) is listed as not judged
  (D397). The wording of the request, the schema and the checks are designed, checked at no cost and reviewed before any send
  (D408).
- **Supersedes:** D399 (the request teaches how to build an event's five states) and, with it, the five states of an event in
  the clean ladder step; D404's rule on naming a theme's five states has nothing left to apply to.
- **Evidence put to him:** five states for the company are faulted by both reader families in 10 of 17 ladders, yes/no in 2 of
  24; of the seven gaps both found, six sit in the division beyond three outcomes and one in a Yes that needs a confirmation
  its No does not. The council's dissent (several outcomes where needed) was put to him as the third option.
- **Scope:** the clean path's ladder step.

## D410 · 2026-11-10 · A group named in a judged question and not listed member by member is not a fault of the question

- **Asked:** "题目里写“四大云厂商”（the big four hyperscalers）但没有列出是哪四家，算不算“问题没说清楚”？严的读者判不合格，松的读者和我认为这是通用叫法。按裁决“问错题”的 11 份里有 8 份是这一类，所以需要你定一个读法，下次两家读者才能按同一把尺子评。"
  - Options: not a fault (recommended): "行业里通用的叫法可以直接用，不要求列出成员。按这个读法，这 8 份不再算“问错题”。"; a fault, the members must be listed.

  group's members. The form says so before the next reading.
- **Not decided by this:** the other boundary cases the two reader families read differently (round log §69, council `iv`).
- **Scope:** the Stage A reading form of the clean ladder step.

## D411 · 2026-11-10 · An amount already reported may be the baseline of a ladder, labelled as that and never as the market's expectation

- **Asked:** "文章只给了“已经公布的数字”（例如英伟达现有采购承诺 1190 亿美元），没有说市场预期明年是多少。这个已公布的数字能不能用来当分档的比较基准？现在模型把它填进了“市场预期”一栏，两家读者都判这是错的。"
  - Options: usable when labelled (recommended): "可以拿来当基准，但明确标成“最近一次已公布的数字”，不再叫“市场预期”；文章给的是区间（如 50%–60%）时也允许填区间。这需要改答案格式，我会放在事件题之后单独做、单独验证。"; not usable (a reference only when the article states an expectation).

  article states as a range is carried as a range. This changes the answer's shape; it is built and measured after the event
  answers (D408), on its own.
- **Scope:** the clean path's ladder step.

## D420 · 2026-11-10 · A proceeding that formally ends without the conclusion the question asks for is ruled out; the question stays

- **Asked:** "题目问的是“法国竞争管理局会不会在 2027 年 1 月 31 日前公布对英伟达反垄断调查的结论”。到期前可能有三种情况：① 公布结案决定（哪怕不处罚），算“发生了”；③ 调查还在继续，算“还在等”。这两点没有争议。有争议的是 ②：当局正式宣布放弃或撤回调查，但没有公布题目问的那种结论。模型每次写法不一样，读者也各执一词。② 算什么？"
  - Options: it is ruled out (recommended): "题目保持原样，问的仍是“有没有公布结论”。这类题固定有三种结果：公布了／当局正式放弃且没有结论／还在查。这也是目前多数已存答案的写法，且符合现有规则“判题目点名追踪的那件事”。不写“明确落空”的答案将算错。"; ask instead whether the investigation is over (two outcomes; it tracks another event than the conclusion the thesis names).
  - Alex: "② 算“明确落空” (Recommended)".
- **Decided:** for a proceeding an authority conducts and whose asked-for event is its published decision or conclusion: a
  published closing decision, with or without a penalty, is the event happened; the authority formally abandoning or
  withdrawing the proceeding without that decision or conclusion is the event ruled out; the proceeding still going on the due
  day is the wait. Such an event always has a ruling out, and an answer that names none, or that writes the authority's
  decision to go on as the ruling out, is at fault. The judged question stays the one the thesis's outcome names.
- **Scope:** the clean path's ladder step; mark R of the readers' form.

## D449 · 2026-11-13 · The wiring's code review: four structural rules, two changes to the run states (council consensus under D439)

- **Council** (`clean-arch/step1-unfiled-2026-11-08/council/mo-handoff.md`, `mo-codex.md` to `mo-codex-3.md`; Claude's notes
  `mo-claude.md`, challenges `mo-challenge-1.md`, `mo-challenge-2.md`): an independent read-only code review of the D448 wiring found eight
  defects, each confirmed against the code (a helper's internal retry could send after a stop; a killed child was redoable; an
  orchestrator's death was found only on its own relaunch; local stops were not shared; the ladder and judge reserved 1 × bytes instead of
  the agreed 2 × bytes + 4,096; launch inputs were not persisted; zero or negative usage could settle a paid request at nothing; the proof
  did not run the real orchestration). Consensus: "agree to build and prove at $0, with the stale-registration relaunch race closed before
  implementation"; the four rules close the eight findings.
- **Decided (rules):** R1, a stop is shared where it is decided (the ladder step's and the judge's final stops and local cap refusals stop
  the shared ledger), and every actual send in a budgeted process reads it first (a stop gate on `urllib.request.urlopen`, installed by
  each entry point; a 403 no component retries); an attempt admitted before a stop may finish. R2, the draw record holds its identity (kind,
  label, ledger, options; a differing launch is refused) and the outcome class (a signal exit is a crash); the launcher is alive while it
  holds its lock, registered on the ledger (the registration is checked under the ledger's lock before the launcher takes its own lock,
  and the gate stops the ledger when a registered lock is free, so an orphaned child's next send and every other draw's are refused).
  R3, every shared language-model reservation is the agreed bound, and the ledger settles a missing, zero, negative or non-finite charge
  at the reservation. R4, the proof runs the real orchestration with a trap in every child process.
- **Decided (changes to WIRING-DESIGN.md §D, not readings of it):** (a) the one redo of Step 1, Step 2 and production is a relaunch with
  `--redo` and a required `--redo-reason` written to the record, made only when the component's output shows an eligible failure (a
  transport failure after its own retries, an answer refused or not fitting its schema); otherwise the run stops; the ladder step and the
  judge have no outer redo (the judge keeps its own inside `run_stage_b`). (b) A crash stops the whole run. `run_stage_b.py`'s inner
  path (a first folder with no outcome, then the redo folder) is unreachable through `run_fresh.py` and is not claimed to satisfy the crash
  rule on its own.
- **Done ($0):** `run_fresh.py`, `budget_replay.py`, the hooks, the entry points; `test_run_fresh.py` 23 tests,
  `test_shared_ledger_hooks.py` 5, `check_budget.py` 16 checks, with mutants for each new rule; `proof_wiring.py` 10 of 10 (a wrong ladder
  archive now caught by the row comparison), `proof_interception.py` 8 of 8 (with a stop during each helper's retry pause and byte-for-byte
  controls for the ladder step, the judge and production), `proof_end_to_end.py` 3 of 3 (one day through the real orchestrator: 5 child
  processes, 55 calls, all reserved, ledger attempts = calls; a SIGKILLed child; a SIGKILLed orchestrator whose child's next send is
  refused). Next: the council's last read of the code and the proof outputs, then the slice by its own decision.
- **Rounds 4–7** (`mo-codex-4.md` to `mo-codex-7.md`): three more findings, all from one mechanism (the order of steps when the launcher
  ends abnormally: a death between the stale probe and the new lock; an unexpected error that unregistered before stopping; the stop
  written after waiting for the child; a signal between saving `started` and the flag; an interruption between components). After the
  third, the findings were no longer answered one by one (AGENTS §1): **R5, fail closed** — the probe, the launcher's lock and its
  registration are one ledger-locked step (`claim_launcher`); every exit of a launch goes through `Draw.close`, where any exit of a launch
  that began work other than a normal return, and any exit leaving an attempt `started` on disk, writes the shared stop first, then ends
  the child, then marks the draw; the registration is removed only after a normal end, a refusal before any work, or that stop, so a
  failed stop leaves it for the gate. `test_run_fresh.py` 30 tests, each new rule with its mutant; `proof_end_to_end.py` 3 of 3; full
  suite 287. **Consensus (round 7): "Council position: ready for the slice."**

  rung; the class counted over p1–p3 and q1–q3 (the q draws identified as another day) by path and field; the same facts' path in the clean
  draws, attributing delivery to Step 2 only after tracing its role. **Falsifiers:** the facts do not bear on the actual questions, were
  unavailable in time, reached the judge another way, or share no cause across the counted cases. The comparison is evidence relevant to
  D427, not acceptance. Before any send: the mechanism, its counted class, the expected effect on the final judgement, a council round.
  Opening stays out of scope until established and decided.

## D483 · 2026-11-14 · Deep reflection council (mw): the way to production is a use-oriented acceptance, prepared on stored runs first; to Alex

- **Asked** (Alex, 2026-11-14): "你重新深度的跑一次council，看所有的trace,深度反思，讨论达到concensus, 然后对齐方向朝向production".
- **Council** (`clean-arch/step1-unfiled-2026-11-08/council/mw-claude-reflection.md`, `mw-codex-1.md`, `mw-codex-2.md`; a fresh Codex read the record
  cold first): the last stretch (D439–D482, nine measured changes, none adopted) moved nothing because each round picked an angle from the last
  round's leftovers and judged it by the seven graded key questions, which both systems fail about equally and which cannot rank them; the
  product mechanism is that one call must decide what to ask, its scope, its years and where facts go, so local rules interact. Weaker than they
  look: "every loss is at opening" holds for the seven key questions only; "no eligible judgement wrong" likewise; Stage B's last judgements
  missed the strictest reading (3 of 24) beside 19 insufficient; unlinked facts cost no answer in this window only.
- **Consensus (a recommendation for Alex, not decided):** "同意以新增的用户价值验收作为通向生产的下一方向；先用两套系统的历史记录做一次 $0 准备测试，验证漏题、事实送达和读者
  校准是否可测。冻结标准和既有生产条件保持有效，新验收及其通过线由 Alex 决定。"
  - The acceptance, an addition beside the frozen ruler: fresh articles unused by any run; both systems the same days from an empty library;
    blind readers who first list from the articles the big questions an analyst would hold (so missed questions count), then judge each
    system's questions (big bet, duplicate, trivia), its judgements (supported by what was available that day; outcomes checked apart), the
    dates, speakers and citations, and facts kept or dropped that would change a judgement; readers calibrated on known cases, disputes
    reported, key disputes ruled by Alex or an investment reader he names; lines, runs, budget and stops fixed before the run.
  - The preparation ($0): on the stored runs of both systems, a bounded set of articles: missed big questions, facts not delivered and with
    no later repeat, with delivered and unrelated controls; it measures whether the readings can be done, their workload and the readers'
    agreement, and declares no winner.
  - Unchanged: the frozen ruler and scores; Stage A not passed; production the default (not declared production-ready); a good result in the new
    acceptance does not by itself change any existing gate.
- **Only Alex:** whether to open the acceptance, its scope and lines, and which pipeline goes forward after it.

## D514 · 2026-11-15 · Correction to D513's wording of the look-back rule (found by the reflection council, round 4)

- **D513 said** that when a question opens "every earlier statement with no link is judged against it" and that "a statement already
  linked to another question is not reconsidered". **The code's rule** (`clean-arch/step3/library.py`, `link_later`) is on groups and
  on how the original arrived: the step checks the earlier groups (a statement with its repeats) whose **original statement arrived
  without a question**; a group whose original arrived under another question is excluded even if the new question also needs it; a
  group that arrived without a question and was linked later is still checked against the next question that opens. A batch that
  fails twice stays pending and is tried again on the next write (none stayed pending in the week's run).
- **Unchanged:** seven calls, 516 group-and-question checks, 2 links; the missing statement of D508's third pair (judge-side id
  e379, the group `163:e3` in the stored library) arrived linked to the export question and so was excluded when the RTX Pro 5500
  question opened. The five pages' correction notes and the status page carry the corrected wording.
- **Also bounded, on the reviewer's reading of D456:** production "does not link an earlier record to a question opened later" (a
  later article repeating the fact can still deliver it), and D456's finding that unlinked facts cost no final answer holds for the
  eligible graded questions of the July window in those six draws, not for unlinked facts in general.

## D559 · 2026-11-15 · Core-problem council (Alex's request): the product problem is forming answerable questions; the clean measurements examined start from empty, against the start-state record of 2026-11-05; one confirmation and one small test go to Alex (council consensus)

  answered and followed: a worthwhile matter is left without an answerable question, or a delivered question asks a materially
  different or potentially unresolvable thing. No single cause is proven. *Where the measurements stood:* the clean
  measurements examined (the three July runs, the weeks of 09-22 and 10-06) each begin with an empty start, which the
  2026-11-05 record says does not represent the specified test with an existing research library.
- **Evidence, all at $0 on the ledgers (reader sessions' cost unknown).**
  - The three July runs (same 14 days, each from empty), two reader families apart (`brief-same-question.md`,
    `tally-output.txt`, `tally-extra.txt`): both grouped the 40 topics into the same 18 matters. The same judged question in
    every run that opened it: 3 (2026 capital spending, the French inquiry, supply commitments), Vera Rubin disputed on one
    attempt. Delivered in every run but different: 3 (China's H200: permission against recorded revenue; credit support: date,
    scope, ranges; Kyber: 2027 against 2028). A question in one run and a refusal in another: 4 (memory prices, the H100
    rental price, federal spending, the Intel stake). Refused in both: 1 (the China-share survey, right by D417). Opened by
    one run of three: 6. Read beside D476 and D477's source review, four of the refusals are topics the first step should not
    have opened; the readers of this review saw no article for this task.
  - The two later weeks, two families apart with each topic's whole opening article (`brief-coverage.md`,
    `tally-coverage-output.txt`): of the 20 topics opened from empty, 18 are on a standing matter and 2 on a new one; 16 were
    opened from an article that mentions the matter in passing (news about it 3, split 1); 10 are on a matter an earlier-dated
    library already held a question on (same question or same matter, in the sealed library of news to 2026-08-28 or in the
    week of 09-22's own topics; 4 by neither family, 6 by one). These classify 20 selected topics; they are not a rate.
  - One case read first-hand: a 4,949-character general piece (2026-10-06) with one sentence on the big five's planned
    spending in 2026 and 2027; from empty the system opened one topic for both years and all three attempts refused it; the
    July runs each formed the 2026 question, and the sealed library holds both years as two questions. What the system would
    do with that library in view is not tested.
- **My own claims the council refused or the readers did not bear out:** the split "the news states the yardstick, so the
  question is the same" (`PREDICTIONS.md`: not shown; both families call 7 of 40 topics "stated"); "the choice of what to
  follow is mostly sound" (withdrawn against D477); "3 of 12 the same" as one number; "the loop cannot close it without
  Alex"; "the weakest act in its hardest condition"; "nothing has measured the product condition"; the 2026 cloud-spending
  matter as three different questions (it is the same judged question in all three runs).
- **The 2026-11-05 record, now given a number.** `docs/CURRENT_STATE.md`: "Start-state correction (2026-11-05): Alex requires a
  research library established from real material available before the test start, then extraction against that state. The
  prior empty-library diagnostic cannot represent this case." Its source is that day's account in
  `../hivemind-no-preseed-evidence-review/docs/research/2026-11-05-parallel-refinement/own-mistakes-2026-11-05.zh.md` ("用户
  2026-11-05 的测试要求：先确保测试起始日之前建立真实题库，再跑抽取；按实际题库是否已有主题判断开题，单独检查证据"), a paraphrase written
  that day; his quoted words of that day are the opening rule: "金标定义的是这个值不值得作为一个主题；existing 题, then don't open ->
  correct；not existing 题, open -> correct". D395 is his later approval of three empty-start draws to measure self-opening
  ("跑，只跑新系统三份"); it supports that diagnostic and replaces nothing. The account of 11-05 was not carried into D466's
  framing or D469's provisional choice, and the lean path's weeks followed D469. Not confirmed by Alex in his own words as a

## D593 · 2026-11-16 · The live-store operating contract, version 9, is agreed for its $0 proof build on test stores; live operation is not authorized (council rounds 111 to 119)

- **The contract** (`docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/live-service/OPERATING-CONTRACT.md`), built through nine versions,
  each answering the council's findings. Its rows:
  1. WAL mode, side files on local disk, `mode=ro`, a loud failure when the store cannot be opened, busy retries.
  2. One read transaction per API request and per MCP tool call, with one connection per call.
  3. One bound resolver (`service.resolve_bound`) for all 13 sites. A future explicit bound is refused; a structural check enforces
     it.
  4. The first day refused everywhere.
  4a. Search: lexical ranking over the visible corpus only, and an index that publishes a day, keyed by store identity, view, text
      hash and model, with staged refreshes. Published vectors are used only for the matching store identity and text.
  5. Checkpoints: what is guaranteed and what is not, a stop after 3 failed truncations, a free-space minimum, and the full-disk
     behaviour.
  6. A crash: committed partial-day writes stay invisible past the last completed day, and the writer does not resume.
  7. A writer lock named by the store's device and inode in one fail-closed lock folder, taken by the writer before it writes and by
     preflight before it copies; one name per store (symlinks resolved, hard links refused); an orderly stop.
  8. AGENTS §9 stays in force. P1 (the product's own readers may read a live WAL store) is a proposed decision, not assumed by any
     proof.
- **Stated limits:**
  - a hand-deleted lock file is detected at the next check point, not prevented;
  - a path swapped away and back around an open is excluded by the operating precondition, not detected;
  - production's own writer takes no lock, and §9 still protects it;
  - no byte bound on the `-wal` within an unfinished day.
- **Decided (D439):**
  - The proof build of the plan's tests (proofs 1 to 10) is next, on test stores only, at $0.
  - It comes back to the council before anything runs live.
  - The proof reports that the checks detect the specified single replacements and does not claim the excluded case is safe.
- **Council (round 119):** "Yes: version 9 is ready for the $0 proof build … this agreement covers test stores, not live operation."

## D598 · 2026-11-16 · Slice 4b built and proven at $0: one writer per store by an operating-system lock, preflight's one locked copy, a snapshot route that never replaces, and the writer leaving WAL mode on every exit (council rounds 134 to 136)

- **Built** (uncommitted; nothing restarted or deployed; P1 still only proposed, so nothing here authorizes a live service):
  - **`src/hivemind/live_lock.py`:**
    - the lock folder, refused when unusable;
    - `acquire`: a store's real path, hard links refused, an `flock` named by device and inode, taken without waiting;
    - `verify`: the path and the lock file still the locked ones, with no new hard link;
    - `snapshot`: the backup API from a read-only source into a temporary file, taken out of WAL mode, integrity checked, and
      published by a hard link that never replaces.
  - **The writer** (`ladder_adapter`):
    - creates its store, locks it, and checks that the locked file is the one it created before the first write;
    - checks the path before each day, stopping with the reason;
    - owns its connection and lock on every exit, closing the connection, after leaving WAL mode when no reader holds it, before
      releasing the lock.
  - **Preflight:** one locked copy of each store, made before any part runs, taken out of WAL mode; a copy from a path that changed
    is discarded.
  - **`scripts/snapshot_store.py`:** the snapshot route's entry point.
  - **The tests' lock folder** is a temporary one (both conftests).
- **Proven:**
  - `tests/test_live_lock.py` (12) and `clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/test_writer_lock.py` (14):
    - aliases and hard links;
    - both start races;
    - paths replaced after the stat, during a copy, between creation and lock, and during the run;
    - an unusable lock folder;
    - every exit, including both opening failures, closing before releasing and leaving the store out of WAL mode;
    - a writer process killed with `SIGKILL` on its third day: the operating system released the lock, and preflight's copy
      answers as the second day;
    - a snapshot taken beside the writer holding uncheckpointed commits: whole, read-only readable, out of WAL mode;
    - the snapshot's refusals, nothing left behind;
    - preflight's entry point handing its parts only the locked copy.
  - The suite passes (339), the new system's folders (186), and the frozen-piece checks. Mutants: 17 of 17 caught
    (`live-service/lock-mutants.txt`).
  - **The filesystem-full proof, run separately on its own disk images:**
    - with the free-space stop off, the disk filled inside the tenth day, the writer crashed, nine days were kept and served, and
      the lock was free;
    - with the stop as built, it stopped before the first day with its reason.
- **Found and fixed in the same slice** (contract, "Found while building 4b"):
  - a WAL-mode store with no side files cannot be opened read-only, so the writer now leaves WAL mode on every exit;
  - preflight's second, unlocked read of each store;
  - `verify` now names a missing store or a new hard link.
- **My errors:**
  - a test fixture first made the very WAL state no read-only reader can open;
  - an after-open failure test first failed inside `acquire`'s own check, because I had not read that `acquire` calls `verify`;
  - the first filesystem-full run shared one disk between both variants, so B could not start.

## D661 · 2026-11-17 · Open defect: the Codex-family blind readers ran with Codex memories on, which carry project context

- **Found** while closing the reader environment for the new control-line reference (design version 7, §4).

  hivemind, its judge, its gold, or Kyber? If you remember nothing, reply exactly NOTHING":
  - with memories on, it answered from memory: "a collision judge … a golden-v5 evaluation baseline";

  project context. That covers the Stage A and Stage B readers, the reference-control readers, the paired test's readers (D656), and the third
  readers and reviewers. Their blindness is weaker than assumed. Whether a given reading was affected depends on what the memory store held on
  its date, and that is not reconstructed.

  - No past result is relabelled now. This is recorded as an open defect.
  - Every new blind Codex reading runs with the three flags and the memory probe (as the new reference's design §4 does).
  - A census of the affected readings (by date, launcher and whether a family's verdict was decisive) is queued after the new reference. Council
    reviews, which are not blind, are unaffected by design.

- **Why the six lines stop blocking:**
  - D400 wrote them for "this first measurement" and told Alex they "不能证明它比老系统好". D548, a council decision, made them gate 1.
  - D560 found no measured link between them and the final answer.
  - Their zero-fault forms are a poor target at the measured luna-era rates (D623): zero faults in 131 sends has even odds only near 0.5% a send.
  - Reader agreement on disputed points is 21 of 70 and 29 of 53, and draws move from 7 failures to 1 (D650).
- **Decided:** as written in `clean-arch/PRD.md` §1.5, which now owns the rule.
  1. **The product comparison is the release decision.**
     - poc-v118 is replayed against the hashed new system (astra-frozen; v5.5 excluded). Both start from empty over 07-01 to 07-19, three draws
       each, and are scored on unread weeks from 07-20 up to 09-20, as far as the full exposure census supports. The exclusion list is frozen.
     - **The main quantity:** big matters served, paired per matter.
     - **Verdicts:**
       - **Practical lead:** a − b ≥ max(3, 15% of N) and a ≥ 2b. Every guardrail subgroup must meet its frozen minimum and pass under both split
         countings.
       - **Practical loss:** the mirror, or a guardrail breach confirmed under both countings.
       - **No practical winner, too small or invalid**, as written.
     - **Guardrails:** unsupported shares (figure and yes/no apart) and the not-worth-tracking share, each within 10 points of the old system's.
       D428's limits are printed beside them.
     - **Illustrative only:** a sign test and an interval.
     - **Frozen and hashed before the first send:** the matter list (blind), the credit rules (one cutoff per matter, the grouping of repeats,
       what counts as the same question), the controls, the versions and the rule.
  2. **What changes, explicitly:**
     - D548's use of D400's six lines as a release gate is superseded. The lines are reported on every ladder run.
     - The parts code decides stay hard: figure ranges meet end to end; the favourable end is stable; the due day is consistent at D400's 90%.
     - D431's frozen-reference reading of 07-01 to 07-14 is still produced and printed beside the comparison, not deciding. D665 supersedes D431
       on that point only.
     - Step 2's three checks stay as D427 and D431 set them.
     - Gate 2's unsupported lines become the guardrails, and its control line waits (D658).
     - Gate 4 folds in.
     - Gate 5 waits for a practical lead and Alex's word.
     - The absolute floors stay proposals, reported beside.
  3. **Back to Alex,** before any release engineering resumes: a practical lead (with the split cards for his spot check), a practical loss at
     once, no practical winner, too small or invalid, or no verdict by 2026-12-01.
- **Next:**
  - the comparison's design at $0: the exposure census, the frozen matter list and credit rules, the cards and controls, the replay plan and
    its spend guard;
  - council review;
  - then a send on Alex's word. No budget is required (D664).

## D675 · 2026-11-18 · Under D672: the reading tools' review found them not ready; fixed, and the frozen rule's open readings written down (before any output)

- **Found** by the council review D672 requires (Codex thread `tools-review-codex.md`; a fresh Claude reader), both "not ready", before any
  comparison output was read. Every finding was checked against the code it cites before a change.
- **Fixed** (`stage0/`; tests 30, in-memory mutants 16 of 16 caught with assertions, `mutants-reading-tools.txt`):
  - the scorer refused nothing short of six draws, and compared the 10-point bar in floating point (12/30 against 9/30 came out a breach);
  - a plant both readers rejected with different labels made the reading invalid;
  - the new system's judge store was always the first attempt, never D449's redo; an incomplete draw was not refused;
  - a missing third-reader mark became a split; an id a reader made up was skipped, then crashed the deck; the reader decided which of a
    duplicate pair was the later one;
  - the systems' raw ids differ in form (the new system's have gaps), so libraries now carry neutral ids Q1..Qn in opening order;
  - the debate prompt did not resend the marks' definitions to closed sessions, and could read a mark of its own round; readings could
    skip the debate;
  - a plant could land on a one-rung ladder; the deck's shuffle seed differed from the card spec's;
  - the card labelled the speaker as the publisher and cut quotes at their first line break (829 stored judge requests of both systems now
    parse to their stated item counts, 248 items with line breaks kept whole, 59 speakers holding a semicolon).
- **Readings of the frozen rule, written here before any output:**
  - **Guardrail shares:** the random sample's cards that cover no matter, as the rule's words say ("covering cards are not in the
    shares"). Codex read it so; the Claude reader called it open; taken as written.
  - **The 10-point bar** is compared exactly; exactly 10 points is not a breach.
  - **A plant** is explicitly rejected when every mark its readers left is unsupported or insufficient, split between the two or not.
  - **Mapping readers see question texts, not the news.** The prompt's "the news supports" is dropped: a different deadline or period for
    the same outcome is opened or narrower. Week reading A2 showed each question's opening article; six libraries of dozens of questions
    cannot carry them, and this difference is disclosed with the result.
- **The card form check is closed:** its second round named only the systems' own content (how many rungs a question has, how many
  questions a library holds), which the card shows as written (D673).
- **Round 2 (both readers "not ready" again; `tools-review-codex-2.md` and a fresh Claude reader), fixed the same day:**
  - **Eligibility is checked by code** (`stage0/eligibility.py`): six complete draws under their own labels, launched within one hour,
    every stored call within 72 h of the first launch (D667). It also records each store's sha256. Export refuses without a passing
    check or with a changed store. Readings carry the fingerprints of the matter list, the mapping, the eligibility check and the deck key.
    The scorer refuses another matter list. Neither the export nor the deck overwrites an existing key.
  - **Mapping answers are void when:** `opened` names no id, or `narrower` lacks the main-outcome judgement. Third readers also see the
    article the question was opened from (week reading A2's form; Codex's ask, for coverage that turns on a date or period).
  - **Cards show each item's publisher,** taken from the item database by the item's input id (card-spec 3). 73 of 73 slice lines
    resolve.
  - **Debate rounds:**
    - a field both families agreed on stays settled, and only disputed fields are debated (and named);
    - a reason may run to at most 40 words;
    - an empty answer written as the string "null" is null.
  - **Plants:**
    - a plant moves the stored rung one place;
    - it enters the deck only when a separate closed reader confirms the moved answer is not supported, as supported controls are confirmed
      supported first;
    - every confirmation is kept beside the key.
  - **More readings of the frozen rule:**
    - a sampled card whose cover the third readers split is resolved per counting like any cover (covers > does not cover);
    - a supported control counts as accepted only when it is marked supported, so a split is not accepted;
    - a repeat counts as the same only when both its final marks equal the original card's, splits included;
    - how each counting resolved every split is printed beside the verdict.
  - **Correction of the record above:** "16 of 16 caught with assertions" was wrong.
    - One mutant was caught by a `KeyError`, not by its assertion. Its test is fixed.
    - The mutant runner now fails loudly when a mutant's text no longer matches the code. Two stale mutants had passed silently as
      "caught". This was found on rerun.
  - **Now:** 41 tests; 28 mutants and 5 controls, all as predicted, each mutant failing its own assertion
    (`stage0/mutants-reading-tools.txt`).
- **Round 3** (Codex in `tools-review-codex-3.md`, plus a fresh Claude reader; both "not ready"), fixed the same day:
  - **Eligibility:** a draw must carry exactly the identity `launch_comparison.py` registers (kind, ledger, items database, manifest,
    07-01 to 09-20, three passes; for the new system also the limits, astra-frozen and the judge to 09-20). All six live draws match.
    The 72-hour window also counts every attempt in the draw's ledger, because a failed send leaves no archive row.

    - the matter rows must equal the frozen list;
    - the mapping file must match its fingerprint and equal the readings' mapping;
    - the eligibility file must pass and must be the one the mapping names;
    - the deck key's product cards must be the readings' cards.

  - **The card:**

  - **Confirmed:** our writer's output passes the entry check, and well-formed results match the parent byte for byte across all five

    - a split stored as an object;

    - A split must be a list of two marks.
    - A cover must be a JSON boolean or "split".
    - Duplicate counts may not exceed ids.

  - a null first-day map, a null mapping entry, or a list used as a question id;
  - a split of two identical marks, which turned a lead into no winner in memory;
  - `company_figure: 1`.

  This was the sixth round in a row with findings from one mechanism, so I stopped patching cases (AGENTS §1). The structural rule:
  `validate_readings` now walks the whole readings file top down, as one closed contract, and checks each container's type before
  reading it. Its docstring lists every shape, which is exactly what `mark_cards.readings` writes:
  - a split is two different marks;
  - flags are JSON booleans;
  - a mapping entry is exactly `{question, covers: true or "split"}`, naming a carded question;
  - the six draws are checked here (folded in from `verdict`);
  - the inputs are seven text fields.

  It runs before `verify_inputs`, so neither can crash on a malformed file.

  Results: 95 tests; 59 mutants, all as predicted (three stale ones repointed); the chain dry run passes the check.

  - a missing first-day map, or a card missing `opened`, which silently dropped opening delays;
  - a named input path that is a directory, which crashed.

  Fixed:
  - The contract now requires the full first-day map, keyed exactly by the listed matters, and every card's nullable `opened`. This is
    what `mark_cards.readings` always writes, and the chain dry run passes.
  - `verify_inputs` turns any failure to read a named file as its writer wrote it into a refusal.

  Now at 96 tests and 62 mutants, all as predicted.
- **Round 18 (Codex, `tools-review-codex-18.md`):** a well-formed but edited readings file could flip a verdict. Codex turned one answered card into "no answer" and the verdict went from loss to lead. Changed opening and first-article days were also accepted. Separately, a draw that opened no question was refused instead of scored as too small, because the writer left out its card map.
  - **Structural rule, one owner:** the scorer no longer scores a readings file it is handed. `score_comparison.score(mapping out, marks folder)` builds the readings with their one writer, `mark_cards.build_readings`, from the named inputs, scores what it built, and refuses a `readings.json` that differs. The command line uses this entry, and so does the chain dry run.
  - **The deck key now decides two more card fields:** each card's answered flag and its opening day. Every draw keeps a card map, empty when the draw opened no question.
  - **Results:** 99 tests; 66 mutants, all as predicted; the chain dry run reaches its verdict through the new entry.
  - **Updated:** the step-4 command in CURRENT_STATE.
- **Round 19 (Codex, `tools-review-codex-19.md`).** Editing any derived file in the chain could still change a verdict:
  - adding one to `distinct.ids` in `mapping.json` turned too small into a lead;
  - moving a deck key's opening day changed the delay printed beside the verdict.

  This happens because the readings record is rewritten from the edited file by its own writer, so the two agree.

  **Structural rule:** the verdict is a function of the primary data only.
  - **Primary data:** the run stores, the readers' own answers (mapping, third reader, control confirmations, card marks) and the
    frozen inputs.
  - **The rebuild:** before scoring, `score_comparison.score(run root, mapping out, marks folder)` rebuilds every derived file in a
    temporary folder with the same code that wrote it (`rebuild.differences`):
    - the eligibility check, through one writer `eligibility.write`;
    - the libraries and the mapping key;
    - `mapping.json`;
    - the deck key and the card texts.

    The rebuild replays the deck's reader confirmations from their record and calls no reader. The scorer refuses if any stored
    derived file differs.
  - **Checks:** the chain dry run now runs in process and restores what it replaces. It scores the unedited chain, and refuses an
    edited mapping, deck key or card text, each with the readings record rewritten as Codex did.
  - **A test leak, fixed:** `seal` had left the scorer pointing at a test matter list. An autouse fixture now restores it.
  - **Totals:** 101 tests; 71 mutants, all as predicted.
- **Round 20 (Codex, `tools-review-codex-20.md`).** The round-19 rebuild still read the stored files after comparing them. Codex
  reported three problems:
  - a file changed between the check and the scoring could still flip a verdict, and stored key order could reorder the printed reasons;
  - fresh imports left additions to the import path;
  - rebuild progress went to stdout, so the command line printed more than the verdict.

  Fixes:
  - `rebuild.scored` now computes the verdict on the readings built from the rebuilt snapshot, while the snapshot still exists, and never
    reads the stored files for it. The stored derived files, including the readings record, are records only: one that differs is
    refused.
  - Progress goes to stderr, and the import path is restored.

  Checks:
  - The dry run edits each derived file twice: once with the record rewritten from the edit, once without. Both are refused.
  - It shows the verdict reads only the snapshot, that stdout carries no progress, and that the import path is unchanged.
  - 101 tests and 74 mutants, all as predicted.
- **Round 21 (Codex, `tools-review-codex-21.md`):**
  - **No change to a verdict or a printed value remains** from edits to stored derived files.
  - **A gap remained in restoring the import path.** The scorer imported before saving the path, and a failure during setup (a missing
    confirmation record) left six entries on it.
  - **Fix:** both `score` and `rebuild.scored` now save the path before their first import and restore it on every exit.
  - **The dry run now also checks a failed setup.** Results: 101 tests and 75 mutants, all as predicted.
- **Round 22 (Codex, `tools-review-codex-22.md`): READY.**
  - The import path is restored on every exit.
  - Every check confirmed in round 21 still holds: the verdict is computed only on the rebuilt snapshot, an edited record is refused, and rebuild progress stays off stdout.
  - The scorer and the rebuild are closed for this run. They next run on the full run's outputs, in the CURRENT_STATE order.

## D676 · 2026-11-19 · The release comparison: the new system loses for two known mechanisms; keep the old system; the outcome was computable before the run (council consensus)

- **Alex:** "did you measure wrong or what … you go deep into the entire trace and logic and run council loop to reason on this
  comparison and the runs of the two system".
- **Council:**
  - an independent cold Codex read (`docs/research/2026-11-19-comparison-review/council-a-codex.md`);
  - Claude's reflection, written first (`claude-reflection.md`);
  - one challenge round (`council-b-codex.md`).
- **Agreed:**
  - **The measurement is sound for the products as configured.**
    - The matter list was built blind from the articles.
    - The mapping was blind with third readers.
    - The controls pass, 13 of 13.
    - The old system's served cards hold on the ones read.
    - No new question was mapped out wrongly.
    - Codex found the old system's Anthropic serve generous; without it b is 6 or 7, still a loss.
  - **Mechanism 1, by design (D382, D384, D505):** the company's own figures are not questions. 7 of the 32 matters are such figures,
    and the old system serves 4 to 6 of them. By D384, five other companies' standalone figures are also outside the new system's
    rules, so its ceiling is 20 of 32 matters.
  - **Mechanism 2, a hand-off defect known since D432:**
    - Step 1 opens bundled questions (two years, or several outcomes), and the frozen ladder refuses them. new-2 lost 27 of 60 and new-3
      19 of 60.
    - Among them are four-hyperscaler capex (M04) and the Anthropic investment (M17) in both runs, and Hugging Face (M19) in new-2.
    - The judge uses pass 1's ladders; new-3's capex question got a valid ladder only on pass 3.
  - **The ceiling ($0 check):** with every dropped key-matter question repaired and served, new is 5–6 against old 10, a = 0, b = 4–5:
    no practical winner, never a lead. Only NVIDIA's own figures (M06, M10, M11, M18) remain.
  - **Process failure:** the attainable verdict was computable in minutes before the run, from the frozen list, D505, D432 and the D489
    week. Neither the council (D665–D667) nor Claude computed it (AGENTS §7.2); two days and about $145 measured a knowable result.
- **Decided (council consensus):**
  - The old system stays for release.
  - No further comparison run.
  - The new path continues only on Alex's word, and only after two things: his D382 call for such a comparison, and a cents-level test
    of the one-outcome hand-off repair on the stored no-ladder cases.
  - Before any future paid comparison, its attainable verdict is computed first.

## D696 · 2026-11-21 · Alex keeps the July test's $0.15 limit as a reservation stop priced from each request's size

- **The question** (after council R round 11, `docs/research/2026-11-20-production-readiness/dependency-design/codex-r11.md`): the budget
  transport reserves, before each model call, a worst case priced from the request's size (2 x its bytes + 4,096 input tokens, the full
  output cap) and refuses a call that would pass $0.15. Over 6,853 stored calls the charge never passed 31% of that reservation, but
  OpenAI publishes no bound tying a request's tokens to its size; its only published input bound (922,000 tokens) would reserve about
  $0.12 a call and make the test impossible under $0.15. Expected total about $0.09. Options: reserve from the request's size
  (recommended); or do not run.
- **Alex's answer** (2026-11-21): "按请求长度预扣 (推荐)".
- **Also fixed on council R's round-11 finding** (verified against the stored usage and the published pricing page, read 2026-11-21):
  gpt-6-luna bills cache writes at $0.125 per million tokens (1.25x input); every stored judge response reports `cache_write_tokens`.
  The July harness settles at the three published input rates (`july_test.settled_llm_cost`: the stored 07-10 Data Center call $0.002895,
  not $0.002662) and reserves each Jev request at TypeSafe's published 64K per-request limit for each of its three attempts. The
  product's own `model.call` cost records omit the cache-write premium too: a cost-reporting finding, recorded, not changed here.

- **Alex's words** (2026-11-22): "work with counsel and have a look at the traces of this problem … what is wrong with the system design

  - figures labelled by the judge (source, calculation, assumption; scope and period);
  - code checks only identity and arithmetic (figure in quote, recompute, part within whole, one value per shared quantity, a sourced
    reference);
  - unreconciled forecasts shown as unresolved;
  - extraction unchanged;

## D731 · 2026-11-22 · judging-v13's paid-gate harness is ready to send (council round 47h); the first attempt is scored on both arms; the ceiling is Alex's

- **What was built (D730):** `research/2026-11-22-number-answers/paid_gate.py` (plan, send, recover, packets, verdict, replay),
  `paid_rehearsal.py` (the provider stubbed at urllib beneath the real budget transport), `paid_mutants.py`; the plan is pinned
  (`paid-plan.sha256`, 6f81dae5…). Record: `PAID-GATE.md` §3 to §3h.

  with a rehearsal case and a mutant; round 47h answered "READY TO SEND (once Alex names the ceiling)".
- **Decided by the council (D725's lines unchanged):**
  - The first attempt is scored on both arms. D725 registers the arms "under the same format and checks" and says nothing about
    retries. A joint retry can repair a cross-card conflict that the separate arm sees only after both calls end, so scoring the
    final answers would credit the joint arm with a second chance the separate arm cannot have. Retries are sent after every first
    attempt and read for diagnosis only (`attempts.md`, `retries.jsonl`).
  - The readers' packets hold only what their four questions need, per card the scored answer's passages, figures, recomputed
    outcome, assumptions and card. No attempt history, code decision or check code (a cross-member code would reveal the arm).
  - The text the readers receive commits to the packet-to-unit mapping: a salted key's sha256 is its first line. The verdict renders
    every packet again from the run and refuses any mismatch.
  - The separate arm's two answers are reconciled one to one: a declared shared forecast is unified only when each call holds exactly
    one, with the same value, bounds and unit.
  - Completeness is judged on the scored attempts. The readings are sealed into the run, the verdict is written once, and `replay`
    must reproduce it.
- **Checks:** rehearsal 63 of 63 (three runs); mutants 33 of 33 caught, the control passes; the $0 gate unchanged (87 of 87, gate run 27).
- **Cost, at `hivemind.model.PRICES` (gpt-6-luna $0.10 input, $0.50 output per million tokens; tokens estimated as characters / 4):**
  - the 36 first attempts are about $0.17 at 4,000 output tokens each, and at most $0.39 if every answer used its 16,000-token cap;
  - the budget transport reserves at most $0.039 for one request before sending;
  - so $0.50 covers every scored attempt. Retries come last, and a ceiling stop among them leaves the scored test complete.
